articleTitle: Proposal for Estimation of the Vertical Center of Gravity and the Decoupling Control with 2-DoF for a Maglev Linear Conveyor
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: Due to the advantages of non-friction, low noise, and smooth operation, magnetic levitation (Maglev) traction motors are promising in the transportation industry. Our research group has designed a Transverse Flux Permanent Magnet Linear Synchronous Motor (PMLSM) with attractive electromagnetic suspension(EMS) technology. However, the deviations in the center of gravity always lead to a coupling effect among the degrees of freedom (DoF). This paper proposes a method that estimates the vertical center of gravity. With the increase of the thrust, it could bring very harsh effects on the pitch direction. Meanwhile, we conducted the decoupling control to suppress the coupling effect between thrust and pitch DoF. Eventually, this paper verifies the estimation and the decoupling performance through simulation validations.

articleTitle: Modelling, Control and Position Estimation for Linear Permanent Magnet Actuators
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In this paper, modelling, control and position estimation for a linear electromagnetic actuator with a permanent magnet mover is presented. A hybrid methodology combining analytical and Finite Element Method (FEM) is adopted for modelling of the actuator. An online parameter estimation method is presented for estimating the electrical parameters based on current switching instant sampling. Two controllers are implemented: the Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) and the Proximate Time Optimal Servo Controller (PTOS). Position estimation is realized through the Luenberger Observer.

articleTitle: Vibration Control of Structures by Mass Variation using Magnetic Levitation
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel vibration control method for structures using a mass variation. A magnetic levitated floater is attached to the ceiling of a structure. The ceiling becomes lighter when the floater levitates, and heavier when the floater contacts the ceiling. The vibration can be suppressed by selecting the levitated state when the displacement and velocity of the ceiling are in the same direction and selecting the contact state when the displacement and velocity are in opposite directions. The principle of damping generation is shown, and the effectiveness of the proposed method is experimentally verified.

articleTitle: Using an Analytic-Based Magnetic Charge Fourier Series Model to Study a Magnetic Lead Screw when Operating as a Magnetic Spring
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: - A magnetic charge field analysis approach is presented that models an array of magnets by using a magnetic vector Fourier series representation. Using a Fourier series function enables the magnets' relative permeability to be accounted for and also reduces the computational burden. The accuracy of the presented modelling approach is validated by studying the fields and forces created by a magnetic lead screw when acting as a magnetic spring.

articleTitle: Permanent Magnet Linear Synchronous Motor Mover Position Estimation at Zero and Low Speed Using Eddy Current Loss Equivalent Resistance
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In this paper, an alternative mover position estimation method of permanent magnet linear synchronous motor at zero and low speeds by using high-frequency (HF) signal injection is proposed. PMLSM usually adopts surface-mounted structure, which makes it not have significant saliency. Moreover, due to the long air gap of PMLSM, it is difficult to saturate the stator core with the injection HF signal to obtain the inductance-based saliency. The proposed method is to estimate the mover position by tracking the resistance-based saliency. By injecting HF pulsing voltage, eddy current loss in stator can vary as the mover is in different positions. The spatial variation of eddy current loss induces equivalent asymmetric resistances in mover estimation synchronous frame, which can be tracked as resistance-based saliency. A finite element analysis model of PMLSM is built to investigate the variation of eddy current loss and the saturation of stator when injecting HF voltage. A simulation model is used to verify the performance of resistance-based saliency in sensorless control.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of the Electrodynamic Suspension of an Hyperloop Test Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper deals with the electromagnetic design of a small vehicle designed to be tested in a dedicated vacuum tube. As imposed by the facilities in the tube, the guidance must be passive. Its design is therefore highly dependent on the vehicle dynamic behaviour to ensure that it remains within the limits of its guidance zone. The guidance and levitation are provided by an electrodynamic suspension (EDS) done with a Halbach array interacting with a conductive track. This article mainly focuses on its design and its influence on the dynamic behaviour of the vehicle.

articleTitle: A Moving Magnet Type Linear Synchronous Motor with No End-effect
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper shows you a moving magnet type linear synchronous motor (LSM) with a pneumatic bearing system. This LSM consists of a field magnet of the Halbach array, of which length is equal to even multiple of the pole pitch, and coreless armature coils, which are excited in the range added the pole pitch to the both ends of the Halbach array. This paper will introduce the principle of no end-effect and explain more detail of the LSM.

articleTitle: Multicriteria design of an electromagnetic hammer
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In this paper, a Pareto based multicriteria design procedure for a linear motor driving an electromagnetic demolition hammer is presented. The hammer application requires high dynamical performance as it must deliver at the same time high value of impact energy and frequency of cycle. The uncertain characteristic of the medium on which the hammer head will impact has to be taken into account in an integrated electromechanical model of the system that could guide the control strategy of the supply system. Requirements of the application are stated and some preliminary analysis that lead to the choice of a Linear Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor are described. The integrated electromechanical model, taking into account the modelling of the head impact on the soil is described. Some of the principal results show that the solution is not unique but comes out of a spread of possibilities so that Pareto criterion is used to sort them out. Simulation results obtained on the main operative hammer quantities are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Design Aspects of a Dynamic Inductive Power Transfer System Made of Precast Concrete Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In this article, the development of a dynamic inductive power transfer (DIPT) system for electric vehicles (EV) on highways in concrete construction is presented. The complete design process is outlined. For this purpose, first general requirements from all domains, which are involved, are collected. Dependencies are identified and boundary conditions and constraints are considered to reduce the number of system degrees of freedom. The focus lies on the construction and electromagnetic design of the roadside precasted concrete element and the electromagnetic coupling with the vehicle-side pick-up module.

articleTitle: Hysteresis Modelling and Coercivity Mechanisms in Hard Ferrites
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: Hysteresis modelling of hard ferrites is discussed, as well as the coercivity mechanisms. The effect of the crystallographic texture on the hysteresis shape is discussed. The coercivity is strongly affect by the grain size. The Stoner-Wohlfarth model provides the upper limit for the coercive force. Limitations of the Stoner-Wohlfarth model are discussed.

articleTitle: Real-Time Modeling of Segmented Multiphase Linear Motor with Thyristor and Neutral Connection During the Switching Process
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: The high dimension sate equation and strong non-linearity challenge building the real-time model of the segmented multiphase linear motor (SMLM) with thyristor switch and neutral connection. In this paper, the linear reconstruction transformation and the neutral point current constraints are used to simplify the complex equation of SMLM first. Then, the associated discrete model of the thyristor is applied to avoid iteration calculation during the switching process. At last, the controlled voltage and current sources are implemented to decouple the calculation of thyristor and SMLM in the hardware-in-loop (HIL) platform. The offline simulation and HIL test results demonstrate that the proposed model can precisely reflect the power-switching transient characteristics. This study can provide a validation platform for the switching control strategy of SMLM.

articleTitle: A Study on the Control of Linear Conveyor Module
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In response to the issues of easy spark generation, complex control system, and high cost in the sliding contact power supply used in the linear motor transmission module, this paper establishes a control model for the linear motor unit module, adopts PID control algorithm, and develops a control program for the linear motor transmission line module. The wireless communication module is used to communicate with multiple motors, and wireless power supply technology is used to power multiple linear motors. Through debugging and operating tests on the direct drive flexible transmission line, the repeated positioning accuracy and absolute position accuracy of the direct drive conveyor reached <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 1.6\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 50\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex>., respectively. Compared with the current direct drive conveyors in the market, the repeated positioning accuracy and absolute positioning accuracy have been improved by more than 75%. The control system is applied to the direct drive flexible linear conveyor, and the control effect is good. It can achieve high-precision, flexible and stable conveying of linear conveyors.

articleTitle: Global Optimization of a Complementary and Modular Linear Flux-Switching Permanent Magnet Motor Applied for Urban Rail Transit to Reduce Normal Force
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: Linear flux-switching permanent magnet motors (LFSPM) have outstanding advantages in the urban rail transit, such as higher power factor and higher efficiency compared with linear induction motors (LIM), as well as lower construction cost compared with traditional permanent magnet linear motors (PMLM), since the permanent magnets and armature windings are both located in the short primary mover. Considering that when the LFSPM motor is applied in the rail transit, excessive unilateral normal force will lead to extra energy loss as well as threaten the safety, global optimization with multiple geometry parameters of a complementary and modular LFSPM (CMLFSPM) motor is achieved with the aid of non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) in this paper. Firstly, key geometry parameters are selected through sensitivity analysis. Then, the NSGA-II and finite element analysis (FEA) are applied in global optimization. Finally, this paper demonstrates that after global optimization, the normal force of the CMLFSPM motor can be greatly reduced under the premise of enough traction force.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Analysis of Linear-rotary Two-degree-of-freedom Tubular Generator for Wave Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel 12-slot 10-pole linearrotary two-degree-of-freedom (LR-2DoF) tubular generator for wave power generation, which outer stator adopts flux switching structure, middle rotor consists of separated iron cores and PMs, and inner mover is slotted iron core. First, its structure is introduced and the working principle is fully analyzed. Second, the 3-D finite element (FE) model is erected and simulated based on finite element method (FEM) to verify the validity of the proposed motor structure. Finally, several significant structural parameters are optimized in order to obtain the optimal back electromotive force (EMF), power density and efficiency based on former 3-D FE model.

articleTitle: Calculation of Eddy Current Loss in Permanent Magnets of a Linear Hybrid Stepper Motor for a Conveyor System
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper presents two general methods for semi-analytical calculation of eddy current loss in permanent magnets and compares them to a transient 3-D FEA calculation. A linear hybrid stepper motor for a conveyor belt application serves as an example.

articleTitle: Embedded Absolute Position Detection for Permanent Magnet Linear Motors with Passive Track
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: The absolute position detection scheme proposed in this paper belongs to the group of scale-less or embedded position detection methods. It uses the permanent magnets of the passive track of the permanent magnet (PM) linear motor as sensor target. As true absolute position detection it covers both (i) the position required for commutation and (ii) the position of the mover on the track even after a system shutdown and additional manual user interaction. The low-cost system approach consists of an array of linear Hall sensors mounted at the stator to evaluate the permanent magnet pattern on the passive track. The proposed sensor system is designed and analyzed in simulation and validated with a prototype system.

articleTitle: An Unconventional Approach to Cogging Force Reduction in Linear Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In linear motors, there are three causes of thrust force fluctuations that affect smooth operation. These are (i) the cogging forces (ii) the load dependent force fluctuations and (ii) the end forces resulting from the limited length of the motor. To the various methods that exist to solve this problem, this paper adds an unconventional method that takes advantage of the limited length of the motor. This paper presents a method to minimize cogging force by changing the slot pitch while pole pitch and winding layout remain unchanged. One of the main advantages of this method is that it is easy to apply in motor design and requires hardly any space.

articleTitle: Noise Reduction for Sub-Nanometer Position Stability in High Dynamic Linear Drives
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: High accuracy and high acceleration are initially contradictory requirements for servo drives. Especially for production machines in the semiconductor industry, both dynamics and accuracy are particularly important. In this paper, a motion controller for a linear direct drive is optimized as a whole system. The correlation between dynamics and position stability is shown. Due to the availability of inverters based on wide-bandgap semiconductors as well as high-speed analog-to-digital converters with 18 bit resolution, additional options for control loop design exist. A design approach is presented to decrease position noise with high control loop bandwidth. Based on the theoretical considerations, a standstill position stability of 20 pm is achieved on a test stand with a high-dynamic linear drive using a PWM frequency of 100 kHz.

articleTitle: Latency optimization of magnetic actuator for optics manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: Active magnetic bearings can potentially be used for linear guidance of machine components. However, their performance is limited by the system's latency. Reducing the latency leads to an improved dynamic stiffness of the actuator, and thus to a broader range of applications. Therefore, this paper introduces a study that aims to improve a novel linear electromagnetic actuator used in optics manufacturing. To analyze the latency, a testbed consisting of an electromagnet, a rapid DC current controller, and a real-time prototyping system is built. The latency of individual components is determined, and pertinent factors are identified. By integrating position and current controls, the latency is reduced by more than 75%. Thereby the dynamic stiffness of the magnets is increased.

articleTitle: Control of a Dual-Stage Positioning System Consisting of two Permanent Magnet Linear Motors for High-Precision Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: Dual-stage actuators are used in applications with high requirements for positional accuracy. One of the most widespread types of these actuators uses voice coil motors for fine positioning. In this paper, a control strategy for a dual-stage actuator consisting of two permanent magnet linear motors is investigated. The control strategy is developed based on the mechanical model of dual-stage actuator and consists of a control concept as well as a decoupling algorithm of the two stages by means of a force feedforward control and a Luenberger Disturbance Observer. With this control strategy, the two stages can finally be decoupled from each other and the fine positioner can be linearized so that its control behavior is similar to that of a voice coil motor. With this setup, the position error of a permanent magnet linear motor can be improved significantly compared to a single-stage system also using a disturbance observer.

articleTitle: Practical Numerical Modeling Approach for a Design of a Two-Dimensional Linear Synchronous Actuator
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper proposes the design of a magnetically levitated planar motor, the configuration of a basic numerical method to embody the control concept, and the design procedure for an experimental test rig. This motor is stable in the levitating direction but unstable in the driving direction because it utilizes the repulsive force between the stator permanent magnets and the moving coils. One problem with magnetically levitated planar motors is the time-consuming nature of the three-dimensional finite element analysis. This analysis requires significant computational resources and can result in significant delays in the design process. To address this problem, a less time-consuming method using Gaussian process regression is presented. In addition, the proposed analysis is verified using a test rig equipped with several sensors. These sensors will provide measurements of static force characteristics and flux linkage to evaluate the performance and effectiveness of the motor under various operating conditions.

articleTitle: Comparison of Track Topologies of Permanent Magnet Electrodynamic Suspensions
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: High-speed MAGLEV can rely on electrodynamic suspensions for their levitation. The track, the conductive part of the suspension where eddy currents take place, has a great influence on the forces generated in the system. Different track topologies, either discrete or continuous, have been explored so far, but not globally compared. The paper aims therefore to compare objectively continuous and discrete track topologies based on performance criteria such as the lift-to-drag and lift-to-weight ratios.

articleTitle: Design Optimization of a Linear Wound Field Flux Switching Machine for Dry Gravity Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In this study, a linear wound field flux switching machine (LWF-FSM) is optimized for use in dry gravity energy storage. Energy storage technologies can be used to mitigate uncertainties on the grid due to the increased share of renewable energy sources (RES). In the newly proposed linear electric machine dry gravity energy storage system (LEM-GESS), LEMs are used to raise and lower a 50 ton hexagonal piston iron mass in a shaft to store and discharge energy. A designed LWF-FSM is optimized for power factor and efficiency using a non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II). Other than the low power factor, the results indicate that the LWF-FSM can offer good performance as main drive unit in the dry gravity energy storage system. It is also observed that by step-positioning, the thrust ripple can be further reduced.

articleTitle: A Suppresing Impact Current Method with Symmetrical Switching for Segmented Linear Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: The impact current limits the speed improvement of the segmented dual three-phase linear motor (SDTPLM). This paper first analyzes the generation mechanism of impact current. Secondly, recording the previous stator's zero-crossing time and sequence and using it to turn on the next stator can suppress the impact current caused by the zero-state response. Then, the impact current caused by the stator parallel connection is suppressed by using a thyristor to turn off in advance, and a suppresing impact current method with symmetrical switching for the SDTPLM is proposed. Finally, the results in MATLAB/Simulink indicate that the proposed method can suppress the 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> impact current by the traditional switching method to 10.54%.

articleTitle: Online Maximum Torque Per Total Ampere Control for Nest-loop Secondary Linear Doubly-Fed Machine Considering Static End Effect
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: The nest-loop secondary linear doubly-fed machine (NLS-LDFM) is a novel linear machine developed from rotary brushless doubly-fed induction machine, which has a potential application in urban rail transit. In this paper, a maximum torque per total ampere (MTPTA) control strategy for NLS-LDFM considering static end effect is proposed. By realizing the MTPTA, the primary copper loss can be reduced. Furthermore, the compensation strategy for static end effect is applied in the control period to reduce the harmonic of current. Finally, the proposed method is verified by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a Capacitor-self-excited Linear Eddy Current Brake for Railway Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: A linear eddy-current brake is used for a type of braking device for railway vehicles that generates the braking force without mechanical contact. The authors proposed a self-excited linear eddy current brake using capacitors. In this paper, the performance of the linear eddy current brake with gap width variation is shown in a bench test using a full-scale armature.

articleTitle: Studying the Peak Force of Magnetic Linear Motion Devices Using Dimensional Neutrality
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: The merits of different sizing equations for linear motion magnetic force devices are assessed. A peak force scaling analysis for a linear magnetic coupling with respect to the volumetric force density, mass force density, magnetic shear stress and energy density is compared. By utilizing a 3-D analytic based model of a Halbach cylinder magnetic coupling it is shown that the maximizing of volumetric and mass force density is not an appropriate sizing metric for a linear magnetic actuator. Only energy density and magnetic shear stress are dimensionally neutral sizing metrics for linear actuators.

articleTitle: Hall-Effect Sensor Based Position Sensor for Force Control of a Bendable Tubular Linear Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper deals with the implementation of a Hall-Effect sensor based linear position sensor for bendable tubular linear synchronous motors. The sensor is analyzed with Finite Element Analysis and a prototype is studied experimentally. The analysis proofs the functionality of the sensor. Using the prototype, a simple open-loop force controller is realized.

Author Keywords: Permanent Magnet Tubular Linear Synchronous Motor

articleTitle: Research on Cylindrical Linear Induction Motor for Drive Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: The control rod drive mechanism (CRDM) is a kind of servo mechanism for the reactor control system of the nuclear power plant. This paper presents a cylindrical linear induction motor suitable for the CRDM. First, the structure of the CRDM is introduced. Second, the relationship between the main dimensions and the electromagnetic load is derived. Third, the influence of materials of the mover shielding shell, speed, and electromagnetic parameters on the lifting force is analyzed by the finite-element method (FEM). Meanwhile, the steady-state temperature of each component of the CRDM is obtained. Finally, a scaled-down prototype is manufactured to verify the rationality of the design. The test results show that the FEM results are consistent with the experimental results, and the essential functions such as lifting, lower insertion, and maintenance can be realized.

articleTitle: Design of a Linear Synchronous Reluctance Motor with Concentrated Windings
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper concerns modeling, design optimization and experimental validation of a linear synchronous reluctance motor with concentrated windings. A synchronous reluctance motor is optimized using a multi-level, sequential Taguchi optimization method. Experimental validation of the models is performed on a secondary that is optimized to be used together with a primary of an existing iron core motor. The measured continuous force and power factor show a deviation with respect to the models of 6.3% and 2.4% respectively. The optimal design achieves a modeled force density of 0.17 N/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and a force ripple of 36.3% for a current density of 7.7 ARMs/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>•

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Magnetic Field Modulation Magnetic Lead Screw for Wave Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of large volume and low power density of the direct drive wave generator, a high-speed magnetic screw for wave power generation is designed in this paper. First, the basic working principle of the magnetic field modulation magnetic lead screw is introduced. The conditions for satisfying the magnetic field modulation are given. The force and torque of magnetic lead screws with different numbers of pole pairs are calculated. Secondly, in order to further increase the power density of the generator, the electromagnetic performance of the magnetic lead screw with different transmission ratios is calculated when the inner permanent magnet has one pair of poles. The influence law of the lead on the distortion rate of the torque waveform and the transmission ratio is obtained. Finally, the power density and electromagnetic performance were comprehensively considered to determine the basic parameters of the magnetic lead screw for wave power generation. The magnetic density distribution of the designed magnetic field modulation magnetic screw is calculated, which verifies the rationality of the design. This design provides a reference for further improving the power density of current wave generators.

articleTitle: Characteristics Verification of Simultaneous Propulsion and Levitation Control of a Linear Induction Motor by Dual Frequency Superimposed Drive
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel magnetic levitation transmission system using a linear induction motor alone. In this system, two frequency components are superimposed to perform simultaneous control. One controls the propulsive force and the other controls the levitation force. The proposed system is expected to save space and cost.

articleTitle: A Multi-Step Model Predictive Direct Thrust Control Method for Linear Synchronous Motors Driven by Three-Level NPC Inverters
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: The standard direct thrust control (DTC) method is not suitable for multi-level inverters and is difficult to deal with complex constraints. In this article, a new prediction model is proposed. It has low computational complexity. Based on this prediction model, a new multi-step model predictive direct thrust control (MP-DTC) method for high-power linear synchronous motors (LSM) is designed. In order to reduce the switching frequency and control the neutral point voltage of three-level neutral-point-clamped (NPC) inverters, new constraint conditions and value functions are designed. Compared to the traditional MP-DTC, the proposed two-step MP-DTC strategy proposed in this article can reduce the switching frequency by 43%. In addition, this method can effectively suppress the neutral point voltage unbalance of three-level NPC inverters in a convenient way. The mean absolute deviation is 1.88%.

articleTitle: Design of a Magnetic Lead Screw with Discretized PMs for Wave Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In order to further improve the power density of wave generators, a magnetic screw used in wave power generation is proposed. In both axial and circumferential planes, the magnetic screw has a magnetic field modulation effect. Based on the speed-up effect of the magnetic gear, the traditional magnetic screw is further improved to increase the speed of the wave generator. It is difficult to manufacture helical permanent magnets. Therefore, the structural parts of the magnetic screw need to be equivalently simplified. The effects of different inner permanent magnets, outer permanent magnets and modulators on the torque and thrust of the magnetic lead screw are investigated. Based on the comparison and analysis of the calculation results, the structure and parameters of the magnetic screw with good electromagnetic performance and easy processing are determined. The flux density for the optimal design is calculated and analyzed. The effectiveness of the magnetic screw designed in this paper for wave power generation is verified.

articleTitle: Discrete Resonant Controller based Current Harmonics Suppression for Dual Three-Phase Linear Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In the electromagnetic propulsion system, the stator current harmonics of linear induction motor will worse control performance and increase loss. Wide range and fast change of frequency make it more difficult to suppress them. This paper proposes a discrete resonant controller based current harmonic suppression strategy. Through the pole correction and phase compensation, the problem of resonance point offset and phase lag caused by discretization and system delay is effectively solved, and the 5th and 7th current harmonics with frequency variation are greatly reduced without increasing the controller bandwidth. The hardware-in-the-loop experiments proved the feasibility and validity of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: Aerodynamic Bearing-Equipped High-Speed PM Motor with Auxiliary Levitation and Extra Torque
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In high-speed motor systems, aerodynamic bearings can generate support to the rotor without external air supply, due to the dynamic pressure effect during the rotor motion. However, there is dry friction between the static and moving surfaces of the bearing before it reaches the lift-off speed. In this paper, it is proposed to add an auxiliary winding in the motor so as to provide auxiliary levitation before lift-off to reduce the dry friction, and then generate extra torque as an additional armature winding while the bearing is working at high speed. The auxiliary winding structure and operation principle are detailed hereafter. Moreover, analytical derivation and finite element method (FEM) verification are elaborated.

articleTitle: Influence of Split Teeth on the Performance of Linear Permanent Magnet Vernier Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In recent years, permanent magnet Vernier motors are popular research objects in electrical machine field. Linear permanent magnet Vernier motor (LPMVM) is a new type of special motor. It works according to the magnetic field modulation mechanism, which can use its own vernier effect to generate greater thrust at low speed. Based on its working principle, three motors are built up and compared in this paper by finite element analysis, while they have different split tooth structures, viz. a non-split-tooth topology, a two-split-teeth one, and a three-split-teeth one. The electromagnetic performances under no-load and on-load conditions are analyzed, focusing on the influence of different structures on thrust and power factor. Finally, it is concluded that the thrust ripple of the motor is weakened by the use of split-teeth, but at the same time, the average thrust of the motor is also reduced. Moreover, the increase of the number of split teeth will reduce the power factor of the motor.

articleTitle: Detent-Force Analysis and Reduction of Modular Permanent-Magnet Linear Synchronous Motors with Non-overlapping Windings
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid method to reduce the detent force of single-sided modular permanent-magnet linear synchronous motors (MPMLSMs) with non-overlapping windings. Firstly, the topology structure of a 6-slot 5-pole MPMLSM with non-overlapping windings is introduced, which the primary consists of several modules. Based on the finite element method (FEM), it is found the main components of the detent force are 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>, 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> and 12<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonics. Secondly, the features and influenced structure parameters of detent force components, cogging force and end force, are analyzed. The 2nd harmonic can be much decreased by adjusting the width and height of end teeth, while the remaining harmonics can be reduced by skewing permanent magnets (PMs). Thirdly, the optimization structures of the former 6s5p MPMLSM are obtained based on FEM. With the hybrid method, the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> harmonic of the detent force has been reduced to 0.41 N, and the peak-to-peak value of the detent force is optimized to 0.94 N. Finally, a prototype is made and tested. The experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: MagLev2-Cobra Linear Drive Harnessing Attraction Forces
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This work presents the operational performance of the MagLev<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-Cobra urban transportation system. Traction and levitation experiments are performed with a single-sided linear induction motor with a long secondary aluminium sheet and solid back-iron. For the levitation, YBCO superconductors refrigerated with Liquid Nitrogen (LN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) inside cryostats running over a magnet rail arranged in Halbach configuration are used. The motor was designed to minimize the attraction force between primary and secondary through repulsive force components. The advantages of the new system are highlighted.

articleTitle: High-performance Sensorless Control Strategy of High-speed Maglev Based on Nonlinear Extended State Observer and Improved Phase Lock Loop
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-performance sensorless control strategy of high-speed maglev based on nonlinear extended state observer and improved phase lock loop (PLL). A NESO with fast convergence speed and strong anti-disturbance ability is proposed to observe the back electromotive force. A Lyapunov function is designed to prove that the NESO can converge to the equilibrium point in a finite time. A disturbance estimation and compensation term is added to the conventional PLL to achieve zero steady-state error tracking when subjecting to a frequency ramp input. Simulation results show that the angle observation error is less than 0.033 rad at 50 km/h and less than 0.1 rad at 600km/h.

articleTitle: Active Magnetic Levitation Bearing Optimization and Dynamic Evaluation for a Hemocompatibility Assessment Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: Long term use of Left Ventricular Assist Devices (LVADs) is often hindered by hemocompatibility and clotting issues. To ameliorate these difficulties, we proposed a Hemocompatibility Assessment Platform (HAP) that can evaluate the hemocompatibility of individual components of LVADs. To eliminate the hemolysis induced by the HAP itself, we developed a Maglev system using a passive magnetic bearing to suspend the rotor radially and an Active Magnetic Bearing (AMB) to control rotor axially. In this study, we evaluated the dynamic performance of the Maglev system. The rotor was successfully levitated and the maximum gap between the Maglev Stator and rotor was 0.25 mm. The stable operating point was at 0.125mm gap. Levitation was stable up to 10 G's and 2000 rpm.

articleTitle: Damping Characteristics of Magnetic Levitation using Bulk Superconductors and Permanent Magnets
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper describes the damping characteristics of the magnetic levitation system using high-temperature superconducting bulks and permanent magnets. Numerical analysis using the combined <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A-V-\varphi$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex> method is performed to investigate the relationship among the superconducting properties, the structure of the levitation system, and the damping characteristics. A superconductor with a smaller critical current density may be used to improve the magnetic damping if the magnetic levitation force is sufficient. An additional electric conductor improves the magnetic damping characteristics. Based on the numerical analysis results, the relationship among them is quantitatively investigated.

articleTitle: Scaling of a Magnetically Levitated Moving-Magnet Planar Motor based on Payload and Pole Pitch
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper considers the scaling of a magnetically levitated moving-magnet planar motor with respect to the pole pitch and payload mass. A semi-analytical optimization based on the harmonic model of the magnet array is used to optimize the magnet height, the coil bundle width, the coil length and the ratio between width of the magnet magnetized in the z-direction and the pole pitch. Afterwards, an analysis of the root mean square acceler-ation of the mover is performed based on a thermal model of each optimized coil. Two scenarios are considered for the optimization. The first scenario limits the horizontal area of the magnet array and examines the range of payload masses for a set of pole pitches. The second scenario fixes the amount of poles in the magnet array and scales the geometry and payload according to the pole pitch.

articleTitle: Linear Induction Motor (LIM) Integrated Propulsion and Levitation MAGLEV via Ladder Type Passive Track
publicationTitle: 2023 14th International Symposium on Linear Drivers for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In an effort to simplify (reduce the cost of) passive track and increase efficiency of existing LIM MAGLEVs with Al on iron passive track+special passive track for guidance and on-board dc controlled electromagnets for levitation&guidance, this paper presents a preliminary electromagnetic design for a LIM integrated propulsion and levitation urban MAGLEV with a single ladder (cage) type track secondary in a tele-cabin like topology. To facilitate the presentation of the design methodology a 16 ton, 20m/s, urban-cabin-like vehicle MAGLEV case study is investigated, to compare with a previous homopolar linear synchronous motor (H-LSM) urban MAGLEV design, with a solid iron segmented passive track, for same specifications.
